parsed.explanation: No criminalisation since 1791 and no documented visitor-facing restriction (no border, document, facility or custody rule reaches travellers), but the combined regime is hostile-without-recourse: no gender-identity recognition, no anti-discrimination or hate-crime framework, and a judiciary documented as non-functional as a protection avenue. The climate evidence — 2018 official hostility finding, concealment-for-safety patterns, harassment in displacement camps, and the unresolved 2019 poisoning death of the national LGBTQ leader — documents societal hostility with thin recourse (tier 3), dated (tier 4). Extrapolating from hostile attitudes plus absent remedies in a thin-data record resolves below the midpoint, but not into High Risk, since no state-enforced universal exposure or organised targeting is documented.

entry_documents.interaction: Nothing in the record addresses passport markers, visa screening or border treatment of trans travellers.

investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Custody placement rules for trans detainees are unresolved; judiciary documented as not functioning as a protection avenue, so any detention would lack recourse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Constitutional guarantees of health, housing, food extend only to citizens, so a visitor cannot invoke them; trans harassment documented in post-2010 displacement camps (dated).
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Disaster-response exclusion patterns (concealment to access housing/healthcare) suggest vulnerability in institutional settings if repeated.

care_services.exposure: No documented visitor-facing care denial; concealment-for-fear impedes service access for LGBTQ residents (dated).
care_services.interaction: HIV data are 2008-era general-population figures; no recent care-access baseline for visitors.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2018 official assessment: hostility toward visibly LGBTI people, particularly the capital; 2017 senate bills would criminalise public advocacy (3 years) and allow certificate denial — lower-house outcome unknown.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Pending bills are resident/organiser-facing; a passed advocacy ban could reach visibly trans visitors engaging publicly.

minors_guardians.exposure: LGBTQ youth face pervasive social hostility; certificate denial bill would affect students (resident-facing).

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Unresolved 2019 death of national LGBTQ organisation president at home, poisoning unconfirmed; high discrimination levels per 2018 reports; no per-capita denominator.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No hate-crime enhancement; judiciary not a functioning recourse; police response not documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Single named incident, dated — weak rate evidence per rubric rules 7/18, but impunity climate corroborates thin recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statutory remedy for trans visitors; no aggravated-penalty framework; no post-Nov-2017 legislative outcome sourced.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin-data jurisdiction: absence of evidence is not safety; hostility-plus-no-recourse structure governs the extrapolation.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A: Vellandra imposes a universal, enforced visitor register and routine exclusion; this jurisdiction documents no visitor-facing state measure at all — its worst documented feature is societal hostility without remedies, not state targeting of travellers.

Below 0.55-B: Kestrel Isles couples friction exposures with written decisions, appeal desks and consular notification that sometimes work; here the judiciary is documented as non-functional as protection, so the same tier of friction carries less recourse. But 0.55-B has a documented universal border exposure this dossier lacks.

Materially below 0.75-C: Meridia has trained border officers, functioning tribunal, compensation for unlawful detention. This jurisdiction has no functioning remedy layer, a hostile 2018 climate finding, and an unresolved lethal 2019 incident — placing it clearly in the Elevated band, not Reduced.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is one of legal silence plus social hostility with no working remedy. No visitor-facing restriction is documented on any axis — no border rule, facility ban, custody rule or criminal statute reaches a trans traveller. But the protections column is empty everywhere, and the record documents hostility toward visibly LGBTI people (2018), concealment as a survival strategy, and an unresolved suspicious death of the national advocacy leader (2019, dated single incident). Under rubric rule 13, a thin dossier with hostile structural signals, absent protections and a non-functioning judiciary resolves toward risk, not the midpoint: the score sits just below 0.50 — Elevated Risk — below remedy-bearing friction jurisdictions like 0.55-B, above any jurisdiction with documented state-enforced visitor exposure like 0.35-A. Uncertainty is high: the pending 2017 bills, custody practice, and current climate after 2019 are all unsourced.
